items.evidence: Vanilla class is RedStoneWireBlock (capital S); the 1.21.7 export says so, but level/classes.rs:227 only knows 'RedstoneWireBlock', so the wire resolves to Class::Block and neighborChanged/onPlace/updateShape/vanilla_signal/interact/placement/survival arms never run. Wire power stays 0, wire emits no signal. Explains both pilot wire-test failures (first assert: power '0' vs '15'; interaction: '0' vs '13'). The wire logic itself matches vanilla method-for-method (power math, getConnectionState dot/line fixups, getConnectingSide, getSignal direction rules) — the fix is a one-line table alias.
items.title: Redstone wire completely non-functional: class-name mismatch means no wire arm ever runs

items.evidence: gameplay-facts.json uses vanilla names NORMAL (21237), DESTROY (6554), BLOCK (91), PUSH_ONLY (64); the loader matches PUSH/POPPED/IMMOVEABLE/IGNORE_ENTITY, so all 27946 states load as PushPull. 335 DESTROY blocks (torches, wire, flowers) are pushed instead of popped; 13 BLOCK blocks (anvils, grindstone, lodestone, piston_head) are pushed instead of blocking; 16 glazed terracottas become pullable by sticky pistons. Explains the torch half of the pilot piston test (torch pushed, no DropResources event).
items.title: Push-reaction loader mapping matches no 1.21.7 value: every state loads as PushPull

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 PistonBaseBlock.isPushable refuses OBSIDIAN, CRYING_OBSIDIAN, RESPAWN_ANCHOR and REINFORCED_DEEPSLATE explicitly before the reaction switch (all four are NORMAL reaction; obsidian hardness 50.0, so the hardness -1 check does not save it). The port has no such check. Explains the obsidian half of the pilot piston test (piston extends and pushes obsidian instead of staying retracted).
items.title: is_pushable lacks vanilla's hardcoded obsidian-family refusal

items.evidence: Vanilla bounds-checks y > maxY (320) and refuses only UP-pushes from y == maxY; the port uses max_y - 1 (319), so it refuses y == 320 outright and refuses UP-pushes from y == 319. A piston at y == 319 pushing up fails in the port where vanilla extends. Floor side matches vanilla exactly.
items.title: is_pushable Y-bound off by one at the ceiling

items.evidence: Vanilla ComparatorBlock.getInputSignal uses the item frame's analog output when a frame is behind the conductor, and the further block's analog output only when there is no frame. The port takes max(frame, block), so it reads higher than vanilla when both exist and the frame is weaker.
items.title: Comparator conductor branch takes max(frame, container); vanilla takes the frame first

items.evidence: Vanilla moveBlocks destroys via Level.destroyBlock (flags 3, neighbour updates fire during the destroy loop) and then runs its explicit updateNeighborsAt loop after the move. The port sets destroyed cells to air with flags 18 (no neighbour updates) and only runs the explicit loop. Final states agree; observable only through BUD/quasi-connectivity timing edge cases.
items.title: Piston-destroyed blocks notify neighbours once; vanilla notifies twice

items.evidence: tools/test_piston_shape_parity.py asserts len(facts['states']) == 35723, so it fails outright on 1.21.7 before comparing anything. The oracle (VanillaPistonShapeOracle) itself is likely fine; the driver constant is the defect.
items.title: Piston-shape driver hardcodes the 26.3 state count (35723); 1.21.7 has 27946

items.evidence: tools/test_projectile_piston_cobweb_parity.py documents in its own docstring that vanilla's second push is 0.01 higher than Horizon's, by the cobweb or not, and deliberately does not compare height. Cause unknown; recorded as a known divergence, not an accepted gap (no cause or owner established).
items.title: Documented 0.01 piston-push height divergence (vanilla's second push higher)

method: javap -c on the named 1.21.7 server jar for every vanilla method in scope, source comparison against versions/1.21.7/crates/, and checks of the prepared 1.21.7 data (block-behaviours.json, gameplay-facts.json). No driver runs and no cargo tests: blocked by the execution-risk notice, and independently the oracles behind the main drivers do not compile for 1.21.7 (O1-O5, Batch 0's scope) and no worktree has .local/minecraft/1.21.7/ for the harness gate. docs/sweep/ does not exist yet (Batch 0's measurement doc had not landed as of 2026-11-22 ~13:00 NPT).
name: Redstone + pistons
out_of_scope_failures: None in Batch 2 scope. The 28 unmapped exported class names (283 exported vs 272 known) were verified exhaustively; only RedStoneWireBlock is Batch 2 scope. Four others fall back to plain Block (FarmBlock, DirtPathBlock, AmethystBlock, SnowyDirtBlock) — flagged for the coordinator / the systematic sweep noted in PORT-NOTES. The experimental redstone evaluator, dispense/dropper behaviours beyond the redstone trigger, and sculk sensors were not verified here.
source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 2 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: redstone ticking, pistons, observers, comparators; 10 drivers + circuit probes; pilot leftovers (3 level::tests). DRAFT: not committed — an execution-risk notice blocks repo execution and git commands without the user's go-ahead.
systemic_note: The three major defects are all data/table mismatches, not logic errors: the wire logic, piston resolver, and signal machinery all match vanilla 1.21.7 method-for-method — but the wire's class name (G7), the push-reaction enum names (G8), and the obsidian hardcode (G9) never reach the correct code paths. G7/G8 are the same bug class as the pilot's tag defects (26.x-shaped tables meeting 1.21.7 data), one level down: the prepared 1.21.7 data is faithful to the jar; the port's lookup tables carry the wrong names.
